seoTitle: Tailscode — Claude Code, Oh My Pi & opencode on iPhone, iPad, Linux & Mac
metaDescription: Native remote for Claude Code, Oh My Pi and opencode over your Tailscale network — a universal iPhone & iPad app with Lock Screen Live Activities, plus open-source GTK4 Linux and macOS desktop clients. Linux is in the AUR and on the App Store. No relay, no account, GPL-3.0.
heroSubhead: Tailscode is a native remote for Claude Code, Oh My Pi and opencode running on your own machines — a universal app for iPhone and iPad with the turn on your Lock Screen, and open-source desktop clients for Linux and the Mac. Point-to-point over your tailnet, no relay, no account.
highlights: Streams every turn live — thinking, tool calls, subagents, code
Approve, answer, and steer the agent without leaving the chat
iPhone, iPad, Linux, and Mac clients built on one shared core
Point-to-point over your Tailscale network — no relay, no tracking

features.title: A real client, not a web view
features.body: Programmatic UIKit on iOS, GTK4 on Linux, AppKit on the Mac, all Swift 6. Streaming transcripts with collapsible thinking and tool groups, and code you copy byte-exact.

features.title: Written, not pasted
features.body: Answers play out of a buffer at a reading pace, a shimmer riding the newest words. Frames come from the display's own clock, and nothing re-wraps under the reader.

features.title: One pill for model and effort
features.body: Which model and how hard it thinks are one decision: tap a level or slide to it, pin a pair, swipe to cycle. Ultracode burns a rainbow along the composer's edge.

features.title: Three agents, one app
features.body: opencode directly, Claude Code through claude-bridge, Oh My Pi through omp-bridge: two open-source companion servers. Every model Oh My Pi can reach is one picker away.

features.title: Steer without stopping
features.body: Queue a follow-up and edit it before it lands, stop a turn, fork it, answer the agent's questions with a tap. Subagents open in place; a compaction is a seam you can read.

features.title: Pictures and clips, made at home
features.body: A Studio on your own ComfyUI machine: the brief, a stage that shows the sketch as it paints, and the machine's shelf. Enhance has a language model of yours write the paragraph.

features.title: Compact by default
features.body: Furniture takes a line, not a card. Tools, thinking and seams rest as one flat line, and a run of links gathers on one rail that opens on hover or tap. Comfortable is a setting.

features.title: Lock Screen status board
features.body: A Live Activity per session shows the phase, elapsed time and tool counts. Finished turns linger with the outcome, and claude-bridge can push updates while the app is suspended.

features.title: Eight themes, two faces each
features.body: One catalog for every client, from Suomi's aurora over a frozen lake to fresh snow by day. Every colour is pushed through a contrast corrector until it clears WCAG.

howItWorks.body: On the machine where you code: opencode serve, claude-bridge in front of Claude Code, or omp-bridge in front of Oh My Pi. All three are open source and take minutes to set up.
Install Tailscale on your devices — free for personal use. They see each other directly; nothing transits anyone else's servers.
Paste an address or let Tailscode discover your servers. Send a prompt from the phone, follow it on the Lock Screen, sit down at the desktop and the same session is already there.

pricing.footnote: One purchase covers iPhone and Mac on the same Apple Account. The Linux client and the Mac build you compile yourself are free, open-source and complete — the unlock is how the work gets funded, not a wall around it.

faq.q: Do I need my own server?
faq.a: Yes, that's the point. Tailscode is a remote for agents running on hardware you control, so there is no middleman cloud: no relay fees, no data sharing, no vendor outage between you and your code. No server yet? Tap 'Try the demo' on the first screen to explore the whole app with sample sessions, no tailnet needed.

faq.q: Which coding agents does it support?
faq.a: opencode natively, 1.x or 2, with any provider you've configured in it; Claude Code through claude-bridge; and Oh My Pi through omp-bridge. The bridges are open-source Swift servers that expose a terminal agent as structured streaming sessions backed by your own subscriptions. Oh My Pi brings its whole provider catalog: Ollama Cloud, OpenCode Go, OpenRouter, Anthropic, xAI, DeepSeek and your local ollama.

faq.q: Is there really a Linux desktop client?
faq.a: Yes: a native GTK4/libadwaita app, plus an AppKit app for macOS 26, in the same repository. Arch users install it from the AUR (`paru -S tailscode`); everyone else grabs the release tarball from GitHub. Both desktops add tiling splits and a global quick-ask hotkey; the Linux client and the Mac build you compile yourself also carry an embedded terminal and web and video panes, which the sandboxed Mac App Store build leaves out.

faq.q: Where do pictures and clips get made?
faq.a: On a machine of yours running ComfyUI, reached over your tailnet: Qwen-Image or FLUX.2 Klein for pictures, LTX for clips. Tailscode is the brief, the stage and the shelf; the files stay in the machine's own output folder, and nothing leaves your tailnet.

faq.q: How do Live Activities update when the app is closed?
faq.a: claude-bridge can push Live Activity updates over APNs, so the Lock Screen keeps ticking — phase, elapsed time, tool counts — even while the app is suspended. Approval requests fire an alert you can act on.

Tailscode Pro is a one-time $14.99 unlock for unlimited servers, the delegate board, concurrent Live Activities on iPhone, and a supporter badge. The free app is the complete core — full chat, permissions, attachments, models, forking, themes, analytics — forever, with one server.

All of it, under GPL-3.0: the iPhone app, both desktop clients, the engine (CodingAgentKit, a Swift 6 package that also runs on Linux), and both bridges (claude-bridge, omp-bridge). Build it yourself or grab it from the App Store.
